correctness.rationale: All quantifiers and boundary cases are handled for an arbitrary commutative Artinian ring, including fields and the zero ring. In every nonzero local Artinian ring every simple ideal L has annihilator m. For a nonsimple ideal C, \(C\subseteq[L:\mathfrak m C]\) while neither L nor mC contains C (Nakayama). If the socle has multiple simple lines, for any simple C choose L different, giving \(C\subseteq[L:0]=\operatorname{Soc}(R)\) while C lies in neither L nor 0. If the socle is simple it lies in every nonzero ideal, and \(I=J=0\) cannot witness failure since \([0:0]=0\). Finite products have coordinatewise coproduct; multi-support ideals are obstructed by splitting their support into I+J and using \(I+J\subseteq[I:J]\). Annihilator images are exactly local maximal ideals and V_c realizes arbitrary subsets. An independent finite-field enumerator exhausts nine finite rings and returned VERIFY_OK. The unrestricted assertion rests on the full proof, not finite experiments.

value.rationale: This determines the complete point set and topology of a recently introduced algebraic spectrum on all commutative Artinian rings, not an unmotivated individual slice. It detects exactly the Gorenstein local factors and gives empty spectra for non-Gorenstein local rings despite their nonempty prime spectra. Mixed products provide a structural contrast to the known dual-ring identification, enabling direct geometric interpretation of the invariant as a Gorenstein locus. The result is exact over arbitrary characteristics and residue-field sizes; its relevance is not premised on downstream conjectural applications. The exhaustive stress-tests include a non-Gorenstein local ring whose maximal ideal has nonzero square, so the phenomenon is not confined to square-zero examples.
